questions.stem:
Under Pick Co.'s job order costing system, manufacturing overhead is applied to work in process using a predetermined annual overhead rate. During January, Pick's transactions included the following:
Direct materials issued to production | $90,000
Indirect materials issued to production | 8,000
Manufacturing overhead incurred | 125,000
Manufacturing overhead applied | 113,000
Direct labor costs | 107,000
Pick had neither beginning nor ending work-in-process inventory. What was the cost of jobs completed in January?
questions.explanation: Cost of jobs completed = direct materials $90,000 + direct labor $107,000 + overhead APPLIED $113,000 = $310,000. Overhead incurred ($125,000) is not used because work in process is charged with applied overhead; the $12,000 difference is underapplied overhead. Indirect materials ($8,000) are already part of overhead, so adding them separately would double count. With no beginning or ending WIP, everything charged to WIP is completed.
questions.explanationJa: 完成品原価 = 直接材料 $90,000 + 直接労務 $107,000 + 製造間接費「配賦額」$113,000 = $310,000。仕掛品に振り替えるのは実際発生額ではなく配賦額なので、実際発生額 $125,000 は使わない（差額 $12,000 は配賦不足）。間接材料 $8,000 は製造間接費に含まれており、別途加算すると二重計上になる。期首・期末仕掛品がないため、仕掛品への集計額がそのまま完成品原価となる。

questions.stem:
DJ Co. has a job-order cost system. The following debits (credits) appeared in the Work in process account for the month of March:
March 1, balance | $12,000
March 31, direct materials | 40,000
March 31, direct labor | 30,000
March 31, manufacturing overhead applied | 27,000
March 31, to finished goods | (100,000)
DJ Co. applies overhead at a predetermined rate of 90% of direct labor cost. Job No. 101, the only job still in process at the end of March, has been charged with manufacturing overhead of $2,250. What was the amount of direct materials charged to Job No. 101?
questions.explanation: Ending WIP = $12,000 + $40,000 + $30,000 + $27,000 - $100,000 = $9,000, all of which belongs to Job 101. Job 101 carries overhead of $2,250, and since overhead is applied at 90% of direct labor, its direct labor = $2,250 / 0.90 = $2,500. Direct materials = $9,000 - $2,500 - $2,250 = $4,250.

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Lap Co.'s Palo Division for the month of April:
Number of | Cost of
units | materials
Beginning work-in-process | 15,000 | $5,500
Started in April | 40,000 | 18,000
Units completed | 42,500
Ending work-in-process | 12,500
All materials are added at the beginning of the process. Using the weighted-average method, the cost per equivalent unit for materials is
questions.explanation: Materials are added at the beginning, so every unit in ending WIP is 100% complete for materials. Weighted-average equivalent units = units completed 42,500 + ending WIP 12,500 = 55,000. Total material cost = $5,500 + $18,000 = $23,500. Cost per equivalent unit = $23,500 / 55,000 = $0.43.
questions.explanationJa: 材料は工程の始点で投入されるため、期末仕掛品も材料については100%完成として扱う。加重平均法の完成品換算量 = 完成品 42,500 + 期末仕掛品 12,500 = 55,000。材料費合計 = $5,500 + $18,000 = $23,500。換算単位あたり原価 = $23,500 ÷ 55,000 = $0.43。

questions.stem: Weighted average and first in, first out (FIFO) equivalent units would be the same in a period when which of the following occurs?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Beginning inventory units equal inventory units.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Both a beginning and an ending inventory exist but are not necessarily equal.

questions.explanation: FIFO separates the work done in the prior period on beginning inventory, while weighted average does not. When no beginning inventory exists there is no prior-period work to separate, so the two methods give identical equivalent units. Ending inventory is treated the same way under both methods, so B is irrelevant; C and D both leave beginning inventory in place, which is exactly what creates the difference.
questions.explanationJa: FIFO法は期首仕掛品に前期投入された作業分を切り離すが、加重平均法は切り離さない。期首仕掛品が存在しなければ切り離す対象がないため、両者の完成品換算量は一致する。期末仕掛品の扱いは両法で同じなのでBは無関係。CとDはいずれも期首仕掛品が存在する状況であり、まさに差異が生じる条件にあたる。

questions.stem:
In process 2, material G is added when a batch is 60% complete. Ending work-in-process units, which are 50% complete, would be included in the computation of equivalent units for
Conversion costs | Material G
questions.explanation: Ending WIP is 50% complete. Material G is added at the 60% point, which these units have not yet reached, so no equivalent units are counted for Material G. Conversion costs are incurred continuously, so the units count as 50% complete for conversion. Hence conversion: Yes, Material G: No.
questions.explanationJa: 期末仕掛品は50%完成。材料Gは60%時点で投入されるが、これらの単位はまだその地点に到達していないため、材料Gの完成品換算量には含めない。一方、加工費は工程を通じて連続的に発生するため、50%分が換算量に含まれる。したがって加工費: Yes、材料G: No。

questions.stem:
During March, Hamilton Company incurred the following costs on Job 10 for the manufacture of 200 motors:
Direct materials | $330
Direct labor | 400
Factory overhead (150% of direct labar) | 600
Original cost accumulation: | $1,330
Direct materials | $50
Direct labor | 80
Direct costs of reworked 10 units: | $130
The rework costs were attributable to exacting specifications of Job 10 and the full rework costs were charged to this specific job. The cost per finished unit of Job 10 was
questions.explanation: Original cost = $1,330. Rework adds direct materials $50 and direct labor $80, and overhead must also be applied to the rework labor at 150%: $80 x 1.5 = $120. Total rework = $50 + $80 + $120 = $250. Total job cost = $1,330 + $250 = $1,580, for 200 units = $7.90 per unit.
questions.explanationJa: 当初原価は $1,330。手直し分は直接材料 $50 と直接労務 $80 に加え、手直しの労務費にも150%の製造間接費を配賦する必要がある（$80 × 1.5 = $120）。手直し原価合計 = $50 + $80 + $120 = $250。総原価 = $1,330 + $250 = $1,580。200個で割ると単位あたり $7.90。間接費の配賦を忘れると $1,460 ÷ 200 = $7.30 となり誤る。

questions.stem: In its April production, Hern Corp., which does not use a standard cost system, incurred total production costs of $900,000, of which Hern attributed $60,000 to normal spoilage and $30,000 to abnormal spoilage. Hern should account for this spoilage as

choices.label: C
choices.text: Period cost of $60,000 and inventoriable cost of $30.000

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inventoriable cost of $60,000 and period cost of $30.000

questions.explanation: Normal spoilage is an unavoidable cost of producing good units, so it stays in inventory as a product cost ($60,000 inventoriable). Abnormal spoilage is avoidable and provides no future benefit, so it is expensed as incurred ($30,000 period cost).
questions.explanationJa: 正常仕損は良品を製造するうえで不可避な原価なので、製品原価として棚卸資産に含める（$60,000 は inventoriable）。異常仕損は回避可能で将来の便益を生まないため、発生時に費用処理する（$30,000 は period cost）。

questions.stem:
The Forming Department is the first of a two-stage production process. Spoilage is identified when the units have completed the Forming process. Costs of spoiled units are assigned to units completed and transferred to the second department in the period spoilage is identified. The following information concerns Forming's conversion costs in May:
Units | Conversion costs
Beginning work-in-process (50% complete) | 2,000 | $10,000
Units started during May | 8,000 | 75,500
Spoilage-normal | 500
Units completed & transferred | 7,000
Ending work-in-process (80% complete) | 2,500
Using the weighted average method, what was Forming's conversion cost transferred to the second production department?
questions.explanation: Spoilage is identified at the end of the Forming process, so normal spoilage counts as 100% complete for conversion. Weighted-average equivalent units = completed 7,000 + normal spoilage 500 + ending WIP 2,500 x 80% (2,000) = 9,500. Total conversion cost = $10,000 + $75,500 = $85,500, so cost per equivalent unit = $85,500 / 9,500 = $9.00. Normal spoilage is charged to the good units transferred out, so the transfer = (7,000 + 500) x $9.00 = $67,500.
questions.explanationJa: 仕損は Forming 工程の完了時点で識別されるため、正常仕損は加工費について100%完成として換算量に含める。加重平均法の完成品換算量 = 完成振替 7,000 + 正常仕損 500 + 期末仕掛品 2,500 × 80%（2,000）= 9,500。加工費合計 = $10,000 + $75,500 = $85,500。換算単位あたり = $85,500 ÷ 9,500 = $9.00。正常仕損の原価は振り替えられる良品に賦課されるため、振替額 = (7,000 + 500) × $9.00 = $67,500。

questions.stem: Mighty, Inc. processes chickens for distribution to major grocery chains. The two major products resulting from the production process are white breast meat and legs. Joint costs of $600,000 are incurred during standard production runs each month, which produce a total of 100,000 pounds of white breast meat and 50,000 pounds of legs. Each pound of white breast meat sells for $2 and each pound of legs sells for $1. If there are no further processing costs incurred after the split-off point, what amount of the joint costs would be allocated to the white breast meat on a relative sales value basis?
questions.explanation: Relative sales value at split-off: white breast meat 100,000 lb x $2 = $200,000; legs 50,000 lb x $1 = $50,000; total $250,000. Joint cost allocated to white breast meat = $600,000 x ($200,000 / $250,000) = $480,000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a basic approach to allocating costs for costing inventory in joint-cost situations?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Physical measures such as weights or volume

choices.label: D
choices.text: Constant gross margin percentage net realizable value method

questions.explanation: The recognized approaches for allocating joint costs are sales value at split-off, physical measures, estimated net realizable value, and the constant gross margin percentage NRV method. Flexible budget amounts are a planning and control tool for variance analysis, not a joint cost allocation basis.
questions.explanationJa: 連結原価の配賦方法として認められているのは、分離点売価法、物量基準、見積正味実現可能価額法、そして一定売上総利益率NRV法である。変動予算額（flexible budget amounts）は差異分析のための計画・統制の道具であり、連結原価の配賦基準ではない。

questions.stem: Kode Co. manufactures a major product that gives rise to a by-product called May. May's only separable cost is a $1 selling cost when a unit is sold for $4. Kode accounts for May's sales by deducting the $3 net amount from the cost of goods sold of the major product. There are no inventories. If Kode were to change its method of accounting for May from a by-product to a joint product, what would be the effect on Kode's overall gross margin?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $1 for each unit of May sold.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $3 for each unit of May sold.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gross margin increases by $4 for each unit of May sold.

questions.explanation: Under the by-product method the net $3 ($4 sales - $1 selling cost) is deducted from cost of goods sold, raising gross margin by $3 per unit. If May is treated as a joint product, its $4 sales price is reported in revenue while the $1 selling cost is a selling expense reported below the gross margin line. Gross margin therefore improves by $4 instead of $3, an increase of $1 per unit sold.
questions.explanationJa: 副産物として処理する場合、純額 $3（売価 $4 − 販売費 $1）を売上原価から控除するため、売上総利益は1単位あたり $3 増える。連産品として処理すると、売価 $4 が売上高に総額で計上される一方、販売費 $1 は売上総利益より下の区分（販売費）に計上される。したがって売上総利益への寄与は $3 ではなく $4 となり、差引き1単位あたり $1 増加する。

questions.stem:
Parat College allocates support department costs to its individual schools using the step method.
Information for May is as follows:
Support departments
Costs incurred | Maintenance | Power
$99,000 | $54,000
Services percentages provided to:
Maintenance | -- | 10%
Power | 20% | --
School of Education | 30% | 20%
School of Technology | 50% | 70%
100% | 100%
What is the amount of May support department costs allocated to the School of Education?
questions.explanation: Under the step method Maintenance is allocated first (it provides 20% to Power while Power provides only 10% back). Maintenance $99,000: to Education 30% = $29,700, to Power 20% = $19,800, to Technology 50% = $49,500. Power now totals $54,000 + $19,800 = $73,800, and is allocated only to the remaining departments, so the 10% back to Maintenance is dropped and the ratios are rescaled over 90%: Education = $73,800 x (20/90) = $16,400. Total allocated to Education = $29,700 + $16,400 = $46,100.
questions.explanationJa: 階梯式配賦法では、他の補助部門への用役提供割合が大きい Maintenance から先に配賦する（Maintenance→Power が20%、Power→Maintenance が10%）。Maintenance $99,000 の配賦: Education 30% = $29,700、Power 20% = $19,800、Technology 50% = $49,500。Power の配賦対象額は $54,000 + $19,800 = $73,800 となる。階梯法では既に配賦済みの Maintenance へは戻さないため、10%を除いた90%で比率を再計算する: Education = $73,800 × (20/90) = $16,400。Education への配賦合計 = $29,700 + $16,400 = $46,100。

questions.stem: Limitations of an activity-based costing system include which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Control of overhead costs is enhanced.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Activity-based costing systems are less reliable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The expense of obtaining cost data is relatively high.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It eliminates arbitrary assignment of overhead costs.

questions.explanation: ABC requires identifying activities, selecting cost drivers, and collecting driver data for each of them, which is costly to build and maintain. A and D describe benefits of ABC rather than limitations, and B is wrong because ABC is generally more reliable than a single plant-wide rate.
questions.explanationJa: ABCは活動の識別、コストドライバーの選定、ドライバーごとのデータ収集を必要とし、その構築と維持にコストがかかる。AとDはABCの限界ではなく利点の記述であり、Bは誤り（ABCは工場全体単一レートより一般に信頼性が高い）。

questions.stem:
Merry Co. has two major categories of factory overhead: material handling and quality control. The costs expected for these categories for the coming year are as follows:
Material handling | $120,000
Quality inspection | 200,000
The plant currently applies overhead based on direct labor hours. The estimated direct labor hours are 80,000 per year. The plant manager is asked to submit a bid and assembles the following data on a proposed job:
Direct materials | $4,000
Direct labor (2,000 hours) | 6,000
What amount is the estimated product cost on the proposed job?
questions.explanation: The plant still applies overhead on direct labor hours, so use the plant-wide rate: total overhead ($120,000 + $200,000) / 80,000 hours = $4 per hour. The job uses 2,000 hours, so overhead = $8,000. Product cost = direct materials $4,000 + direct labor $6,000 + overhead $8,000 = $18,000.
questions.explanationJa: この工場は現在も直接労務時間基準で製造間接費を配賦しているため、工場全体レートを用いる。配賦率 = 製造間接費合計（$120,000 + $200,000）÷ 80,000時間 = $4/時間。当該ジョブは2,000時間なので間接費 = $8,000。製品原価 = 直接材料 $4,000 + 直接労務 $6,000 + 製造間接費 $8,000 = $18,000。

questions.stem: A CPA would recommend implementing an activity-based costing system under which of following circumstances?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The client is a single-product manufacturer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most of the client’s costs currently are classified as direct costs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The client produced products that heterogeneously consume resources.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The client produced many different products that homogeneously consume resources.

questions.explanation: ABC pays off when products consume resources in different proportions, because a single plant-wide rate would then cross-subsidize products. A single product (A) needs no allocation refinement, mostly direct costs (B) leaves little overhead to allocate, and homogeneous consumption (D) means a single rate already gives accurate results.
questions.explanationJa: ABCが有効なのは、製品ごとに資源の消費割合が異なる（heterogeneous）場合である。単一レートでは製品間の内部補助が生じてしまうためである。単一製品（A）では配賦の精緻化が不要、大半が直接費（B）では配賦対象の間接費が少ない、均質に消費する（D）なら単一レートでも十分正確になる。

questions.stem:
Book Co. uses the activity-based costing approach for cost allocation and product costing purposes.
Printing, cutting, and binding functions make up the manufacturing process. Machinery and equipment are arranged in operating cells that produce a complete product starting with raw materials. Which of the following are characteristic of Book's activity-based costing approach?
I. Cost drivers are used as a basis for cost allocation.
II. Costs are accumulated by department or function for purposes of product costing.
III. Activities that do not add value to the product are identified and reduced to the extent possible.
questions.explanation: I is correct: ABC allocates costs using cost drivers. III is correct: identifying and reducing non-value-added activities is a central aim of ABC. II describes traditional costing, which accumulates costs by department or function; ABC accumulates costs by activity, and the cell layout described in the question is itself organized around activities rather than departments.
questions.explanationJa: Iは正しい（ABCはコストドライバーを配賦基準に用いる）。IIIも正しい（付加価値を生まない活動を識別し削減することはABCの中心的な狙い）。IIは伝統的原価計算の説明であり、部門・機能別に原価を集計する。ABCは活動別に集計し、設問のセル生産方式のレイアウト自体も部門ではなく活動を軸に構成されている。

questions.stem:
Boyle, Inc. makes two products, X and Y, that require allocation of indirect manufacturing costs. The following data was compiled by the accountant before making any allocations:
Product X | Product Y
Quantity produced | 10,000 | 20,000
Direct manufacturing labor hours | 15,000 | 5,000
Setup hours | 500 | 1,500
The total cost of setting up manufacturing processes and equipment is $400,000. The company uses a job-costing system with a single indirect cost rata. Under this system, allocated costs were $300,000 and $100,000 for X and Y, respectively. If an activity-based system is used, what would be the allocated costs for each product?
Product X | Product Y
questions.explanation: ABC assigns setup costs using setup hours, not labor hours. Total setup hours = 500 + 1,500 = 2,000. Product X = $400,000 x (500 / 2,000) = $100,000; Product Y = $400,000 x (1,500 / 2,000) = $300,000. This reverses the labor-hour based allocation ($300,000 / $100,000) because Y requires far more setups despite fewer labor hours.
questions.explanationJa: ABCでは段取原価を労務時間ではなく段取時間で配賦する。段取時間合計 = 500 + 1,500 = 2,000時間。製品X = $400,000 × (500 ÷ 2,000) = $100,000、製品Y = $400,000 × (1,500 ÷ 2,000) = $300,000。労務時間基準の配賦（X $300,000 / Y $100,000）とは逆転する。Yは労務時間こそ少ないが段取回数がはるかに多いためである。

questions.stem: In an activity-based costing system, what should be used to assign a department's manufacturing overhead costs to products produced in varying lot sizes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A single cause and effect relationship

choices.label: C
choices.text: Relative net sales values of the products

choices.label: D
choices.text: A product's ability to bear cost allocations

questions.explanation: Products made in varying lot sizes consume batch-level activities (setups, material moves) differently from unit-level activities, so more than one driver is needed. A single relationship (A) cannot capture both levels. Relative sales value (C) and ability to bear cost (D) are not cause-and-effect bases and are inappropriate for ABC.
questions.explanationJa: ロットサイズが異なる製品は、バッチレベルの活動（段取、材料の移動）と単位レベルの活動とで消費の仕方が異なるため、複数のドライバーが必要になる。単一の因果関係（A）では両方のレベルを捉えられない。相対売価（C）や負担能力（D）は因果関係に基づく基準ではなく、ABCには適さない。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information pertaining to 1,200,000 papers that were processed by DEP Company:
Total cost | $1,050,000
Labor cost | $950,000
Labor hours | 190,000
The following processing standards have been set for DEP Co.'s clerical workers:
Number of hours per 1,000 papers processed | 150
Normal number of papers processed per year | 1,600,000
Wage rate per 1,000 papers | $ 750
Standard variable cost of processing 1,600,000 papers | $1,280,000
Fixed costs per year | $ 200,000
DEP Company's expected total cost to process 1,200,000 papers, assuming standard performance, is
questions.explanation: Standard variable cost per paper = $1,280,000 / 1,600,000 = $0.80. For 1,200,000 papers the variable cost = $960,000. Fixed costs are $200,000 per year regardless of volume. Expected total cost = $960,000 + $200,000 = $1,160,000.

questions.stem:
Based on the following information pertaining to 1,200,000 papers that were processed by DEP Company:
Total cost | $1,050,000
Labor cost | $950,000
Labor hours | 190,000
The following processing standards have been set for DEP Co.'s clerical workers:
Number of hours per 1,000 papers processed | 150
Normal number of papers processed per year | 1,600,000
Wage rate per 1,000 papers | $ 750
Standard variable cost of processing 1,600,000 papers | $1,280,000
Fixed costs per year | $ 200,000
DEP's labor rate variance is
questions.explanation: Standard rate per hour = $750 per 1,000 papers / 150 hours per 1,000 papers = $5.00. Actual rate = $950,000 / 190,000 hours = $5.00. Labor rate variance = (actual rate - standard rate) x actual hours = ($5.00 - $5.00) x 190,000 = $0.
questions.explanationJa: 標準賃率 = 1,000枚あたり $750 ÷ 1,000枚あたり150時間 = $5.00/時間。実際賃率 = $950,000 ÷ 190,000時間 = $5.00/時間。労働賃率差異 = (実際賃率 − 標準賃率) × 実際時間 = ($5.00 − $5.00) × 190,000 = $0。両者が一致するため差異は生じない。

questions.stem:
Relevant information for material A follows:
Actual quantity purchased | 6,500 lbs.
Standard quantity allowed | 6,000 lbs.
Actual price | $3.30
Standard price | $4.00
What was the direct material quantity variance for material A?
questions.explanation: The quantity (usage) variance isolates the effect of using more or less input, so it is measured at the STANDARD price: (actual quantity - standard quantity) x standard price = (6,500 - 6,000) x $4.00 = $2,000 unfavorable. The actual price of $3.30 belongs to the price variance and must not be used here.
questions.explanationJa: 数量差異は投入量の多寡だけを切り出すため、必ず「標準」価格で測る。(実際数量 − 標準数量) × 標準価格 = (6,500 − 6,000) × $4.00 = $2,000 の不利差異。実際価格 $3.30 は価格差異で使う数値であり、ここで使うと数量と価格の影響が混ざる。

questions.stem: For the current period production levels, Woodwork Co. budgeted 11,000 board feet of production and purchased 15,000 board feet. The material cost was budgeted at $7 per foot. The actual cost for the period was $8.50 per foot. What was Woodwork's material price variance for the period?
questions.explanation: The material price variance is computed on the quantity PURCHASED, not the quantity budgeted or used: (actual price - standard price) x actual quantity purchased = ($8.50 - $7.00) x 15,000 = $22,500 unfavorable. Using the 11,000 budgeted feet would give $16,500, which is the trap in choice B.
questions.explanationJa: 材料価格差異は「購入量」に対して計算する（予算量や消費量ではない）。(実際価格 − 標準価格) × 実際購入量 = ($8.50 − $7.00) × 15,000 = $22,500 の不利差異。予算の 11,000 board feet を使うと $16,500 となり、これが選択肢Bの誤答パターン。

questions.stem:
Hart Company uses job order costing. Factory overhead is applied to production at a determined rate of 150% of direct-labor cost. Any over- or underapplied factory overhead is closed to the cost of goods sold account at the end of each month
▪ | Job 1001 was the only job in process at the end of April, with accumulated costs as follows:
Direct materials | $4,000
Direct labor | 2,000
Applied factory overhead | 3,000
$9,000
▪ | Jobs 1002, 1003, and 1004 were started during May.
▪ | Direct materials requisitions for May totaled $26,000.

Overhead is charged at the applied rate, not the $32,000 actually incurred. Ending WIP (Job 1004) = $2,800 + $1,800 + ($1,800 x 150% = $2,700) = $7,300. Cost of goods manufactured = $85,000 - $7,300 = $77,700.

questions.stem: The difference between standard hours at standard wage rates and actual hours at standard wage rates is referred to as which of the following types of variances?
questions.explanation: Holding the wage rate constant at standard isolates the effect of hours used, which is the labor usage (efficiency) variance. The labor rate variance instead holds hours constant and varies the rate.
questions.explanationJa: 賃率を標準に固定したまま時間の差を見ているので、労働時間（能率）差異＝labor usage variance にあたる。労働賃率差異はこれと逆で、時間を実際に固定して賃率の差を見る。

questions.stem:
Based on the following inventory balances and manufacturing cost data for the month of January for Summit Company. Under Summit's cost system, any over- or underapplied overhead is closed to the cost of goods sold account at the end of the calendar year.
