Work-in-process | 7,500 | 10,000
Finished goods | 32,000 | 25,000
Month of January
Cost of goods manufactured | $257,500
Factory overhead applied | 75,000
Direct materials used | 95,000
Actual factory overhead | 72,000
What was the total amount of direct-material purchases during January?
questions.explanation: Materials purchased = materials used + ending inventory - beginning inventory = $95,000 + $20,000 - $15,000 = $100,000. Inventory increased by $5,000, so purchases must exceed usage by that amount.
questions.explanationJa: 直接材料購入額 = 消費額 + 期末棚卸 − 期首棚卸 = $95,000 + $20,000 − $15,000 = $100,000。材料棚卸が $5,000 増えているため、購入額は消費額をその分だけ上回る。

questions.stem:
Based on the following inventory balances and manufacturing cost data for the month of January for Summit Company. Under Summit's cost system, any over- or underapplied overhead is closed to the cost of goods sold account at the end of the calendar year.
Inventories: | Beginning | Ending
Direct materials | $15,000 | $20,000
Work-in-process | 7,500 | 10,000
Finished goods | 32,000 | 25,000
Month of January
Cost of goods manufactured | $257,500
Factory overhead applied | 75,000
Direct materials used | 95,000
Actual factory overhead | 72,000
How much direct-labor cost was incurred during January?
questions.explanation: Cost of goods manufactured = beginning WIP + direct materials + direct labor + applied overhead - ending WIP. Substituting: $257,500 = $7,500 + $95,000 + DL + $75,000 - $10,000, so DL = $90,000. Applied overhead ($75,000) is used, not actual ($72,000).
questions.explanationJa: 当期製品製造原価 = 期首仕掛品 + 直接材料 + 直接労務 + 配賦間接費 − 期末仕掛品。代入すると $257,500 = $7,500 + $95,000 + 直接労務 + $75,000 − $10,000 となり、直接労務費 = $90,000。ここで使うのは配賦額 $75,000 であって実際発生額 $72,000 ではない。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to Roe Co.'s June manufacturing operations:
Standard direct labor hours per unit | 2
Actual direct labor hours | 10,500
Number of units produced | 5,000
Standard variable overhead per standard direct labor hour | $3
Actual variable overhead | $28,000
Roe's June unfavorable variable overhead efficiency variance was
questions.explanation: Standard hours allowed = 5,000 units x 2 hours = 10,000. The efficiency variance measures only the hours difference at the standard rate: (10,500 - 10,000) x $3 = $1,500 unfavorable. Actual variable overhead of $28,000 belongs to the spending variance.
questions.explanationJa: 標準許容時間 = 5,000個 × 2時間 = 10,000時間。能率差異は標準配賦率で時間差だけを測る: (10,500 − 10,000) × $3 = $1,500 の不利差異。実際変動間接費 $28,000 は予算（消費）差異で使う数値。

questions.stem: Quick Co. was analyzing variances for one of its operations. The initial budget forecast production of 20,000 units during the year with a variable manufacturing overhead rate of $10 per unit. Quick produced 19,000 units during the year. Actual variable manufacturing costs were $210,000. What amount would be Quick's flexible budget variance for the year?
questions.explanation: The flexible budget is built on ACTUAL output: 19,000 units x $10 = $190,000. Flexible budget variance = actual cost $210,000 - $190,000 = $20,000 unfavorable. Using the original 20,000-unit budget ($200,000) would give $10,000, which confuses the flexible budget variance with the volume difference.
questions.explanationJa: 変動予算は「実際」生産量で組む: 19,000個 × $10 = $190,000。変動予算差異 = 実際変動費 $210,000 − $190,000 = $20,000 の不利差異。当初予算の 20,000個（$200,000）で比べると $10,000 となるが、それは操業度差異を混ぜた計算になる。

questions.stem:
Birk Co. uses a job order cost system. The following debits (credit) appeared in Birk's work-in-process account for the month of April:
April | Description | Amount
1 | Balance | $4,000
30 | Direct materials | 24,000
30 | Direct labor | 16,000
30 | Factory overhead | 12,800
30 | To finished goods | (48,000)
Birk applies overhead to production at a predetermined rate of 80% of direct labor cost. Job No.5, the only job still in process at the end of April, has been charged with direct labor of $2,000. What was the amount of direct materials charged to Job No. 5?
In a job order cost system, the use of direct materials previously purchased usually is recorded as an increase in
questions.explanation: Issuing direct materials moves cost out of stores (materials inventory) and into production, increasing work-in-process control. Stores control decreases. Indirect materials, not direct, would go to factory overhead control.
questions.explanationJa: 直接材料の払い出しは、材料勘定（stores control）から製造現場へ原価を移す取引なので、仕掛品統制勘定（work-in-process control）が増加する。stores control は減少する。製造間接費統制勘定に入るのは間接材料であって直接材料ではない。

questions.stem:
Jonathan Mfg. adopted a job-costing system. For the current year, budgeted cost driver activity levels for direct labor hours and direct labor costs were 20,000 and $100,000, respectively. In addition, budgeted variable and fixed factory overhead were $50,000 and $25,000, respectively. Actual costs and hours for the year were as follows.
Direct labor hours | 21,000
Direct labor costs | $110,000
Machine hours | 35,000
For a particular job, 1,500 direct-labor hours were used. Using direct-labor hours as the cost driver, what amount of overhead should be applied to this job?
questions.explanation: The predetermined rate is set from BUDGETED amounts: (budgeted variable $50,000 + budgeted fixed $25,000) / 20,000 budgeted direct labor hours = $3.75 per hour. Applied to the job = 1,500 hours x $3.75 = $5,625. Actual hours and costs do not enter the rate.
questions.explanationJa: 予定配賦率は「予算」データから決める: (変動費予算 $50,000 + 固定費予算 $25,000) ÷ 予算直接労務時間 20,000時間 = $3.75/時間。当該ジョブへの配賦額 = 1,500時間 × $3.75 = $5,625。実際時間 21,000 や実際労務費 $110,000 は配賦率の計算に入らない。

questions.stem:
A Job order cost system uses a predetermined factory overhead rate based on expected volume and expected fixed cost. At the end of the year, underapplied might be explained by which of the following situations?
Actual volume | Actual fixed costs

choices.label: A
choices.text: Greater than expected | Greater than expected

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greater than expected | Less than expected

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less than expected | Greater than expected

choices.label: D
choices.text: Less than expected | Less than expected

questions.explanation: Underapplied means actual overhead exceeds applied overhead. Applied overhead falls when actual volume is less than expected, and actual overhead rises when actual fixed costs are greater than expected. Both conditions together widen the shortfall, so volume less than expected with fixed costs greater than expected.
questions.explanationJa: 配賦不足（underapplied）とは実際発生額が配賦額を上回る状態。実際操業度が予想を下回れば配賦額が減り、実際固定費が予想を上回れば実際発生額が増える。この2つが重なると差はさらに広がるので、操業度は予想未満・固定費は予想超過の組合せとなる。

questions.stem:
In developing a predetermined factory overhead application rate for use in a process costing system, which of the following could be used in the numerator and denominator?
Numerator | Denominator

choices.label: A
choices.text: Actual factory overhead | Actual machine hours

choices.label: B
choices.text: Actual factory overhead | Estimated machine hours

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estimated factory overhead | Actual machine hours

choices.label: D
choices.text: Estimated factory overhead | Estimated machine hours

questions.explanation: A predetermined rate must be computable before the period begins, so both numerator and denominator are estimates: estimated factory overhead / estimated machine hours. Any combination using actual amounts could not be determined in advance.
questions.explanationJa: 予定配賦率は期首時点で計算できなければならないため、分子・分母とも見積値を用いる（見積製造間接費 ÷ 見積機械時間）。実際値を含む組合せは期首に確定できないので予定配賦率になり得ない。

questions.stem: In a process cost system, the application of factory overhead usually would be recorded as an increase in
questions.explanation: Applying overhead assigns cost to the products being made, so it increases work-in-process inventory control (credit: factory overhead applied). Factory overhead control accumulates the actual costs incurred, not the application.
questions.explanationJa: 製造間接費の配賦は製造中の製品へ原価を割り当てる処理なので、仕掛品統制勘定が増加する（貸方は factory overhead applied）。factory overhead control は実際発生額を集計する勘定であり、配賦の相手ではない。

questions.stem:
Mart Co. adds materials at the beginning of the process in Department M. The following information pertains to units in Department M's work-in-process during April:
Work-in-process, April 1 (60% complete as to conversion cost) | 1,500
Started in April | 12,500
Completed | 10,000
Work-in-process, April 30 (75% complete as to conversion cost) | 4,000
Under the weighted-average method, the equivalent units for conversion cost are
questions.explanation: Under the weighted-average method, equivalent units = units completed + ending WIP x completion. Completed = 10,000 (beginning inventory's prior-period work is not separated), ending WIP = 4,000 x 75% = 3,000. Total = 13,000.
questions.explanationJa: 加重平均法の完成品換算量 = 完成品 + 期末仕掛品 × 完成度。完成品 10,000（加重平均法では期首仕掛品の前期作業分を切り離さない）、期末仕掛品 4,000 × 75% = 3,000。合計 13,000。

questions.stem:
Yarn Co.'s inventories in process were at the following stages of completion at the end of April
No. of units | Percent complete
200 | 90
100 | 80
400 | 10
Equivalent units of production amounted to
questions.explanation: Equivalent units convert partially finished units into whole-unit equivalents: 200 x 90% = 180, 100 x 80% = 80, 400 x 10% = 40. Total = 300. Choice D (700) is the raw unit count with no conversion applied.
questions.explanationJa: 完成品換算量は仕掛中の単位を完成品相当に換算する: 200 × 90% = 180、100 × 80% = 80、400 × 10% = 40。合計 300。選択肢D（700）は換算せずに単位数を合計しただけの誤り。

questions.stem:
Kerner Manufacturing uses a process cost system to manufacture laptop computers. The following information summarizes operations relating to laptop computer model #KJK20 during the quarter ending March 31:
Units
Work-in-process inventory, January 1 | 100
Started during the quarter | 500
Completed during the quarter | 400
Work-in-process inventory, March 31 | 200
Beginning work-in-process inventory was 50% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Ending work-in-process inventory was 75% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Direct labor work-in-process inventory on January 1 was $25,000. Direct labor costs added during the quarter were $360,000. What is the total value of direct labor costs in ending work-in-process inventory using the weighted-average unit cost inventory valuation method?
questions.explanation: Weighted average pools beginning cost with current cost: $25,000 + $360,000 = $385,000. Equivalent units = completed 400 + ending WIP 200 x 75% (150) = 550. Cost per equivalent unit = $385,000 / 550 = $700. Ending WIP = 150 x $700 = $105,000.

questions.stem:
Kerner Manufacturing uses a process cost system to manufacture laptop computers. The following information summarizes operations relating to laptop computer model #KJK20 during the quarter ending March 31:
Units
Work-in-process inventory, January 1 | 100
Started during the quarter | 500
Completed during the quarter | 400
Work-in-process inventory, March 31 | 200
Beginning work-in-process inventory was 50% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Ending work-in-process inventory was 75% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Direct material work-in-process inventory on January 1 was $50,000. Direct material costs added during the quarter were $720,000. What is the total value of material costs in ending work-in-process inventory using the weighted-average unit cost inventory valuation method?
questions.explanation: Weighted average: total material cost = $50,000 + $720,000 = $770,000. Equivalent units = 400 completed + 200 x 75% (150) = 550. Cost per equivalent unit = $770,000 / 550 = $1,400. Ending WIP = 150 x $1,400 = $210,000.

questions.stem:
Kerner Manufacturing uses a process cost system to manufacture laptop computers. The following information summarizes operations relating to laptop computer model #KJK20 during the quarter ending March 31:
Units
Work-in-process inventory, January 1 | 100
Started during the quarter | 500
Completed during the quarter | 400
Work-in-process inventory, March 31 | 200
Beginning work-in-process inventory was 50% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Ending work-in-process inventory was 75% complete for direct materials and direct labor costs.
Direct material work-in-process inventory on January 1 was $50,000. Direct material costs added during the quarter were $720,000. What is the total value of material costs in ending work-in-process inventory using the FIFO unit cost, inventory valuation method?
questions.explanation: FIFO uses only current-period cost and current-period work. Equivalent units = work to finish beginning WIP 100 x (100% - 50%) = 50, plus units started and completed 400 - 100 = 300, plus ending WIP 200 x 75% = 150, giving 500. Cost per equivalent unit = current cost $720,000 / 500 = $1,440. Ending WIP = 150 x $1,440 = $216,000. The $50,000 beginning cost stays with the completed units.
questions.explanationJa: FIFO法は当期に投入した原価と当期の作業だけで単価を出す。完成品換算量 = 期首仕掛品の完成に要した分 100 × (100% − 50%) = 50 + 当期着手完成分 (400 − 100) = 300 + 期末仕掛品 200 × 75% = 150 → 合計 500。換算単位あたり原価 = 当期材料費 $720,000 ÷ 500 = $1,440。期末仕掛品 = 150 × $1,440 = $216,000。期首原価 $50,000 は完成品側に残る。

questions.stem:
During current year, the following manufacturing activity took place for a company's products.
Beginning work-in-process, 70% complete | 10,000 units
Units started into production during the year | 150,000 units
Units completed during the year | 140,000 units
Ending work-in-process, 25% complete | 20,000 units
What was the number of equivalent units produced using the first-in, first-out method?
questions.explanation: FIFO counts only work done this period: finishing beginning WIP 10,000 x (100% - 70%) = 3,000, units started and completed 140,000 - 10,000 = 130,000, and ending WIP 20,000 x 25% = 5,000. Total = 138,000. Weighted average would give 145,000 by not separating the prior-period work.
questions.explanationJa: FIFO法は当期に行った作業だけを数える。期首仕掛品の完成に要した分 10,000 × (100% − 70%) = 3,000、当期着手完成分 140,000 − 10,000 = 130,000、期末仕掛品 20,000 × 25% = 5,000。合計 138,000。加重平均法なら前期作業分を切り離さないため 145,000 になる。

questions.stem: Bing Company had no beginning work-in-process inventory, and the ending work-in-process inventory is 50% complete as to conversion costs. The number of equivalent units as to conversion costs would be

choices.label: A
choices.text: The same as the units completed

choices.label: B
choices.text: The same as the units placed in process

choices.label: C
choices.text: Less than the units placed in process

questions.explanation: With no beginning inventory, units placed in process = units completed + ending WIP. Ending WIP counts only 50% for conversion, so equivalent units are less than the units placed in process but MORE than the units completed. That rules out A, B and D.
questions.explanationJa: 期首仕掛品がないので、投入量 = 完成品 + 期末仕掛品。加工費について期末仕掛品は50%しか数えないため、換算量は投入量より小さくなる。一方で完成品に期末仕掛品の50%分が上乗せされるので、完成品より大きい。したがってA・B・Dはいずれも成立しない。

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using a process costing system versus job-order costing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is difficult to determine cost of goods sold when partial shipments are made before completion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It is difficult to ensure that material and labor are accurately charged to each specific job.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It involves the calculation of stage of completion of goods-in-process and the use of equivalent units.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It is expensive to use as a good deal of clerical work is required.

questions.explanation: Process costing must estimate how far along the units in process are and convert them into equivalent units, which introduces judgment and calculation that job-order costing avoids. A and B describe difficulties of job-order costing, and the heavy clerical work in D is also a job-order trait since costs must be tracked job by job.
questions.explanationJa: 工程別原価計算では仕掛品の進捗度を見積り、完成品換算量に置き換える必要があり、個別原価計算にはない判断と計算が生じる。AとBは個別原価計算側の困難であり、Dの事務負担も、ジョブごとに原価を追跡する個別原価計算の特徴。

questions.stem: Black, Inc. employs a weighted average method in its process costing system. Black's work in process inventory on June 30 consists of 40,000 units. These units are 100% complete with respect to materials and 60% complete with respect to conversion costs. The equivalent unit costs are $5.00 for materials and $7.00 for conversion costs. What is the total cost of the June 30 work in process inventory?
questions.explanation: Materials are 100% complete: 40,000 x $5.00 = $200,000. Conversion is 60% complete: 40,000 x 60% x $7.00 = $168,000. Total ending WIP = $368,000. Treating conversion as 100% complete would give $480,000 (choice D).

questions.stem: In the computation of manufacturing cost per equivalent unit, the weighted-average method of process costing considers

choices.label: A
choices.text: Current cost less cost of beginning work-in-process inventory

choices.label: B
choices.text: Current costs plus cost of ending work-in-process inventory

choices.label: C
choices.text: Current costs plus cost of beginning work-in-process inventory

questions.explanation: The weighted-average method pools the cost already in beginning work-in-process with the costs added this period and spreads the total over all equivalent units. FIFO is the method that uses current costs only (choice D).
questions.explanationJa: 加重平均法は期首仕掛品に含まれる原価と当期投入原価を合算し、その合計を全換算量で割る。当期原価だけを使うのはFIFO法（選択肢D）である。

questions.stem: The sale of scrap from a manufacturing process usually would be recorded as a(an)
questions.explanation: Scrap proceeds recover part of the manufacturing overhead already charged, so the sale is credited to factory overhead control, reducing it. It does not touch finished goods because scrap is a by-product of the process rather than a completed product.
questions.explanationJa: スクラップの売却代金は、既に負担した製造間接費の一部を回収するものなので、製造間接費統制勘定の貸方に計上され同勘定が減少する。スクラップは完成品ではなく工程からの副次的産物なので、製品勘定には影響しない。

questions.stem: A department adds material at the beginning of a process and identifies defective units when the process is 40% complete. At the beginning of the period, there was no work in process. At the end of the period, the number of work-in-process units equaled the number of units transferred to finished goods. If all units in ending work-in-process were 66-2/3% complete, then ending work-in-process should be allocated

choices.label: A
choices.text: 50% of all normal defective unit costs

choices.label: B
choices.text: 40% of all normal defective unit costs

choices.label: C
choices.text: 50% of the material costs and 40% of the conversion costs of all normal defective unit costs

choices.label: D
choices.text: None of the normal defective unit costs

questions.explanation: Defective units are identified at the 40% point. Ending WIP is 66-2/3% complete, so it has already passed the inspection point and must bear a share of normal defect cost. The cost is spread over the units that passed inspection, namely the units transferred out plus ending WIP. Since those two quantities are equal, ending WIP absorbs 50% of the normal defective unit costs.
questions.explanationJa: 仕損は工程の40%時点で識別される。期末仕掛品は66-2/3%完成なので既に検査点を通過しており、正常仕損費を負担しなければならない。正常仕損費は検査点を通過した単位（完成振替分＋期末仕掛品）で按分する。設問ではこの2つの数量が等しいので、期末仕掛品が負担するのは正常仕損費の50%となる。

questions.stem:
Simpson Company manufactures electric drills to the exacting specifications of various customers.
During April, Job 43 for the production of 1,100 drills was completed at the following costs per unit:
Direct materials | $5
Direct labor | 4
Applied factory overhead | 6
$15 Final inspection of Job 43 disclosed 50 defective units and 100 spoiled units. The defective drills were reworked at a total cost of $250, and the spoiled drills were sold to a jobber for $750. What would be the unit cost of the good units produced on Job 43?
questions.explanation: Total cost charged to the job = 1,100 x $15 = $16,500, plus rework of $250 = $16,750. The spoiled units sold for $750, and that recovery reduces the job's cost: $16,750 - $750 = $16,000. Good units = 1,100 - 100 spoiled = 1,000 (the 50 reworked drills are good units). Unit cost = $16,000 / 1,000 = $16.00.
questions.explanationJa: ジョブに集計された原価 = 1,100個 × $15 = $16,500、手直費 $250 を加えて $16,750。仕損品100個を $750 で売却した回収額はジョブの原価から控除する: $16,750 − $750 = $16,000。良品数 = 1,100 − 仕損100 = 1,000個（手直しした50個は良品に戻っている）。単位原価 = $16,000 ÷ 1,000 = $16.00。

questions.stem: During June, Delta Co. experienced scrap, normal spoilage, and abnormal spoilage in its manufacturing process. The cost of units produced includes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Normal spoilage, but neither scrap nor abnormal spoilage

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scrap and normal spoilage, but not abnormal spoilage

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scrap, normal spoilage, and abnormal spoilage

questions.explanation: Scrap and normal spoilage are unavoidable consequences of producing good units, so both remain in the cost of units produced. Abnormal spoilage is avoidable and provides no future benefit, so it is expensed as a period cost rather than being inventoried.
questions.explanationJa: スクラップと正常仕損は良品を製造するうえで避けられない結果なので、いずれも製品原価に残る。異常仕損は回避可能で将来の便益を生まないため、棚卸資産に含めず期間費用として処理する。

questions.stem: Actual sales values at the split-off point for joint products Y and Z are not known. For purposes of allocating joint costs to products Y and Z, the relative sales value at split-off method is used. An increase in the costs beyond split-off occurs for product Z, while those of product Y remain constant. If the selling prices of finished products Y and Z remain constant, the percentage of the total joint costs allocated to product Y and product Z would

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decrease for product Y and increase for product Z

choices.label: B
choices.text: Decrease for product Y and product Z

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase for product Y and product Z

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase for product Y and decrease for product Z

questions.explanation: With no actual split-off values, the allocation base is estimated net realizable value, that is final selling price less costs beyond split-off. Higher separable costs for Z lower Z's net realizable value, so Z's share of the base shrinks and Y's share grows. Joint cost allocated to Y increases and to Z decreases.
questions.explanationJa: 分離点の実際売価が不明なため、配賦基準は見積正味実現可能価額（最終売価 − 分離後費用）となる。Zの分離後費用が増えるとZのNRVが下がり、配賦基準に占めるZの割合が縮小してYの割合が拡大する。したがってYへの配賦は増加し、Zへの配賦は減少する。

questions.stem:
Rome Co. produces two joint products. BEC and CAL. Joint production costs for June were $30,000.
During June, further processing costs beyond the split-off point, needed to convert the products into saleable from, were $25,000 and $35,000 for 800 units of BEC and 400 units of CAL, respectively. BEC sells for $100 per unit, and CAL sells for $200 per unit. Rome uses the net realizable value method for allocating joint product costs. For June, the joint costs allocated to product BEC were
questions.explanation: Net realizable value of BEC = 800 x $100 - $25,000 = $55,000. NRV of CAL = 400 x $200 - $35,000 = $45,000. Total = $100,000. Joint cost to BEC = $30,000 x ($55,000 / $100,000) = $16,500. Allocating on sales value alone ($80,000 each) would split the cost evenly and miss the different separable costs.

questions.stem: A company manufactures two products, X and Y, through a joint process. The joint (common) costs incurred are $500,000 for a standard production run that generates 240,000 gallons of X and 160,000 gallons of Y. X sells for $4.00 per gallon, while Y sells for $6.50 per gallon. If there are no additional processing costs incurred after the split-off point, what is the amount of joint cost for each production run allocated to X on a physical-quantity basis?
questions.explanation: On a physical-quantity basis the selling prices are ignored and only volume matters: X = $500,000 x (240,000 / 400,000 gallons) = $300,000. Relative sales value would give a different answer: X sells for 240,000 x $4.00 = $960,000 and Y for 160,000 x $6.50 = $1,040,000, so X would take $500,000 x ($960,000 / $2,000,000) = $240,000, which is choice B. The question specifies the physical-quantity basis.
questions.explanationJa: 物量基準では売価を無視し数量だけで配賦する: X = $500,000 × (240,000 ÷ 400,000ガロン) = $300,000。相対売価基準では結果が変わり、Xの売価総額 240,000 × $4.00 = $960,000、Yは 160,000 × $6.50 = $1,040,000 なので、Xへの配賦は $500,000 × ($960,000 ÷ $2,000,000) = $240,000 となり選択肢Bになる。設問は物量基準を指定している点を読み落とさないこと。

questions.stem:
The diagram below represents the production and sales relationships of joint products P and Q. Joint costs are incurred until split-off, then separable costs are incurred in refining each product. Market values of P and Q at split-off are used to allocate joint costs.
If the market value of P at split-off increases and all other costs and selling prices remain unchanged, then the gross margin of
P | Q

figure.alt: Diagram of joint products P and Q. Joint costs are incurred up to the split-off point, after which separable costs are added to P and to Q before sale.

questions.explanation: Joint costs are allocated on split-off market values. If P's split-off value rises, P absorbs a larger share of the joint cost while Q absorbs less. Since selling prices are unchanged, P's higher cost lowers its gross margin and Q's lower cost raises its gross margin.
questions.explanationJa: 結合原価は分離点市場価値で配賦される。Pの分離点価値が上がるとPが負担する結合原価の割合が増え、Qの負担は減る。販売価格は不変なので、原価が増えたPの売上総利益は減少し、原価が減ったQの売上総利益は増加する。

questions.stem:
In accounting for by-products, the value of the by-product may be recognized at the time of
Production | Sale
questions.explanation: Both timings are acceptable. Recognizing at production records the by-product at net realizable value as it is created (an inventory asset); recognizing at sale defers recognition until the by-product is sold. Practice permits either, so the answer is yes to both.
questions.explanationJa: どちらの時点も認められる。生産時点で認識する方法は、産出時に正味実現可能価額で副産物を棚卸資産として計上する。販売時点で認識する方法は、売れるまで認識を繰り延べる。実務上いずれも許容されるため、両方Yesとなる。

questions.stem:
The following information pertains to a by-product called Moy:
Sales in July | 5,000 units
Selling price per unit | $6
Selling costs per unit | 2
Processing costs | 0
Inventory of Moy was recorded at net realizable value when produced in June. No units of Moy were produced in July. What amount should be recognized as profit on Moy's July sales?
questions.explanation: Moy was already recorded at net realizable value when produced in June, that is ($6 - $2) x 5,000 = $20,000 carried as inventory. In July the sale brings revenue of $30,000, relieves the $20,000 carrying amount and incurs $10,000 of selling costs, leaving $30,000 - $20,000 - $10,000 = $0. Recording at NRV at production is precisely what removes any profit at the time of sale.
questions.explanationJa: Moyは6月の生産時点で正味実現可能価額、すなわち ($6 − $2) × 5,000 = $20,000 で在庫計上済み。7月の販売では売上 $30,000 が立ち、在庫 $20,000 が払い出され、販売費 $10,000 が発生するので、$30,000 − $20,000 − $10,000 = $0。生産時点でNRV計上する方法は、販売時に利益が出ないようにする処理そのものである。

questions.stem:
Mig Co. produces gasoline and a gasoline by-product. The following information is available pertaining to sales and production of the first year of operations:
Total production costs to split-off point | $120,000
Gasoline sales | 270,000
By-product sales | 30,000
Gasoline inventory, ending | 15,000
Additional by-product costs:
Marketing | 10,000
Production | 15,000
Mig accounts for the by-product at the time of production. What are Mig's cost of sales for gasoline and the by-product for the first year of operations?
Gasoline | By-product
questions.explanation: Recognizing the by-product at production means its net realizable value reduces the joint cost. By-product NRV = $30,000 sales - ($10,000 marketing + $15,000 production) = $5,000. Gasoline cost = $120,000 - $5,000 = $115,000, less ending inventory $15,000 = $100,000 cost of sales. The by-product has no cost of sales because its value was already recognized at production.
questions.explanationJa: 副産物を生産時点で認識する方法では、その正味実現可能価額を結合原価から控除する。副産物NRV = 売上 $30,000 − (販売費 $10,000 + 製造費 $15,000) = $5,000。ガソリンの原価 = $120,000 − $5,000 = $115,000、期末在庫 $15,000 を差し引いて売上原価 $100,000。副産物は生産時点で価値を認識済みのため売上原価は計上されない。

questions.stem:
Alley Co. produces main products Kul and Ju. The process also yields by-product Bef. Net realizable value of by-product Bef is subtracted from joint production cost of Kul and Ju. The following information pertains to production in July at a joint cost of $54,000:
Product | Units produced | Market value | Additional cost after split-off
Kul | 1,000 | $40,000 | $ 0
Ju | 2,500 | $60,000 | $ 0
Bef | 500 | $ 9,000 | $5,000
If Alley uses the net realizable value method for allocating joint cost, how much of the joint cost should be allocated to product Kul?
questions.explanation: The by-product's net realizable value is removed from the joint cost first: Bef NRV = $9,000 - $5,000 = $4,000, so the joint cost to split between the main products is $54,000 - $4,000 = $50,000. Allocating on relative market value of the main products only: Kul $40,000 of ($40,000 + $60,000) = 40%. Kul's share = $50,000 x 40% = $20,000. Forgetting to deduct the by-product NRV would give $21,600.
questions.explanationJa: まず副産物の正味実現可能価額を結合原価から控除する: BefのNRV = $9,000 − $5,000 = $4,000。主産物に配賦する結合原価は $54,000 − $4,000 = $50,000。主産物だけの相対市場価値で配賦する: Kul は $40,000 ÷ ($40,000 + $60,000) = 40%。Kulへの配賦 = $50,000 × 40% = $20,000。副産物のNRV控除を忘れると $21,600 になる。

questions.stem:
Companies in what type of industry may use a standard cost system for cost control?
Mass production industry | Service industry
questions.explanation: Standard costing needs repetitive, measurable activities, not physical products. Mass production obviously qualifies, and service industries can set standards for repetitive tasks such as processing a claim or servicing an account, so both may use it for cost control.
questions.explanationJa: 標準原価計算に必要なのは反復的で測定可能な作業であり、物としての製品ではない。大量生産業が該当するのは当然として、サービス業でも保険金請求の処理や口座対応のような反復業務に標準を設定できるため、どちらも原価管理に利用できる。

questions.stem:
When a manager is concerned with monitoring total cost, total revenue, and net profit conditioned upon the level of productivity, an accountant would normally recommend
Flexible budgeting | Standard costing
questions.explanation: Flexible budgeting restates revenue and cost for the actual level of activity, which is exactly what monitoring results conditioned on productivity requires. Standard costing supplies the per-unit benchmarks that make the flexible budget and its variances meaningful, so both are recommended.
questions.explanationJa: 変動予算は実際の操業度に合わせて収益と原価を組み直すもので、まさに生産性の水準を前提に業績を監視する目的に合う。標準原価計算は、その変動予算と差異分析の基礎となる単位あたりの基準値を与える。したがって両方が推奨される。

questions.stem: A standard cost system may be used in

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neither process costing nor job order costing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Process costing but not job order costing

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either job order costing or process costing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Job order costing but not process costing

questions.explanation: A standard cost system sets predetermined costs per unit and compares them with actual results. That comparison works regardless of how costs are accumulated, so standards can be applied in job order costing and in process costing alike.
questions.explanationJa: 標準原価計算は単位あたりの原価をあらかじめ設定し、実際結果と比較する仕組みである。この比較は原価の集計方法に依存しないため、個別原価計算にも工程別原価計算にも適用できる。

questions.stem:
Fount Company uses a standard cost system. For April, total overhead is budgeted at $80,000 based on the normal capacity of 10,000 direct-labor hours. At standard, each unit of finished product requires two direct-labor hours. The following data are available for April production activity:
Equivalent units of product | 4,750
Direct-labor hours worked | 9,250
Actual total overhead incurred | $79,500
What amount should Fount credit to the applied factory overhead account for April?
questions.explanation: In a standard cost system overhead is applied on STANDARD hours allowed, not hours actually worked. Rate = $80,000 / 10,000 hours = $8.00. Standard hours allowed = 4,750 equivalent units x 2 hours = 9,500. Applied = 9,500 x $8.00 = $76,000. Using the 9,250 actual hours would give $74,000, and the $79,500 actually incurred is the debit to overhead control, not the credit to applied.
questions.explanationJa: 標準原価計算では、間接費は実際作業時間ではなく「標準許容時間」で配賦する。配賦率 = $80,000 ÷ 10,000時間 = $8.00。標準許容時間 = 換算量 4,750個 × 2時間 = 9,500時間。配賦額 = 9,500 × $8.00 = $76,000。実際時間 9,250 を使うと $74,000 となり誤り。実際発生額 $79,500 は間接費統制勘定の借方であって、配賦勘定の貸方ではない。

questions.stem:
Baby Frames, Inc., evaluates manufacturing overhead in its factory by using variance analysis. The following information applies to the month of May:
Actual | Budgeted
Number of frames manufactured | 19,000 | 20,000
Variable overhead costs | $4,100 | $2 per direct labor hour
Fixed overhead costs | $22,000 | $20,000
Direct labor hours | 2,100 hours | 0.1 hour per frame
What is the fixed overhead spending variance?
questions.explanation: The fixed overhead spending (budget) variance compares actual fixed cost with budgeted fixed cost only: $22,000 - $20,000 = $2,000 unfavorable. Production volume does not enter this variance; the 19,000 versus 20,000 frames difference belongs to the volume variance.
questions.explanationJa: 固定費の予算（消費）差異は、実際固定費と予算固定費だけを比べる: $22,000 − $20,000 = $2,000 の不利差異。生産量はこの差異に関係しない。19,000個と20,000個の差は操業度差異で扱う。

questions.stem: Which of the following standard costing variances would be least controllable by a production supervisor?
questions.explanation: The volume variance arises from the difference between the denominator activity used to set the fixed overhead rate and the activity actually attained, which is driven by sales demand and capacity decisions made above the shop floor. Overhead efficiency, labor efficiency and material usage all reflect how the production line consumes inputs, which a supervisor can influence.
questions.explanationJa: 操業度差異は、固定費率を決めるときの基準操業度と実際の操業度との差から生じ、その水準は販売需要や設備能力の意思決定に左右される。これらは製造現場の上位で決まる。一方、間接費能率差異・労働能率差異・材料消費差異は、いずれも製造ラインでの資源の使い方を反映するため監督者が影響を与えられる。

questions.stem:
Rigley Company has underapplied overhead of $55,000 for the calendar year. Before disposition of the underapplied overhead, selected year-end balances from Rigley's accounting records are:
Sales | $1,200,000
Cost of goods sold | 900,000
Direct materials inventory | 150,000
Work-in-process inventory | 200,000
Finished goods inventory | 100,000
Under Rigley's cost accounting system, over or underapplied overhead is allocated to appropriate inventories and cost of goods sold based on year-end balances. In its annual income statement, Rigley should report costs of goods sold as
questions.explanation: Underapplied overhead is prorated over the balances that contain applied overhead: work-in-process $200,000 + finished goods $100,000 + cost of goods sold $900,000 = $1,200,000. Direct materials inventory is excluded because no overhead has been applied to it. Share to cost of goods sold = $55,000 x ($900,000 / $1,200,000) = $41,250, so reported cost of goods sold = $900,000 + $41,250 = $941,250.
questions.explanationJa: 配賦不足額は、配賦間接費を含んでいる残高に按分する: 仕掛品 $200,000 + 製品 $100,000 + 売上原価 $900,000 = $1,200,000。直接材料在庫には間接費が配賦されていないため対象外。売上原価への按分額 = $55,000 × ($900,000 ÷ $1,200,000) = $41,250。したがって計上する売上原価 = $900,000 + $41,250 = $941,250。

questions.stem: To meet its monthly budgeted production goals, Acme Mfg. Co. planned a need for 10,000 widgets at a price of $20 per widget. Acme's actual units were 11,200 at a price of $18.50 per widget. What amount reflects Acme's price variance?
questions.explanation: The price variance is measured on the quantity actually acquired: (actual price - standard price) x actual quantity = ($18.50 - $20.00) x 11,200 = $16,800 favorable. The price paid was below standard, so the variance is favorable. Using the planned 10,000 units would give $15,000 (choice B).
questions.explanationJa: 価格差異は実際に取得した数量に対して測る: (実際価格 − 標準価格) × 実際数量 = ($18.50 − $20.00) × 11,200 = $16,800 の有利差異。支払価格が標準を下回っているので有利差異となる。計画数量 10,000個 を使うと $15,000（選択肢B）になり誤る。

questions.stem:
Which of the following variances would be useful in calling attention to a possible short-term problem in the control of overhead costs?
Spending variance | Volume variance
questions.explanation: The spending variance compares actual overhead with the budget allowance for the activity attained, so it flags cost overruns that management can act on now. The volume variance merely reflects that activity differed from the denominator level used to set the fixed rate; it signals capacity utilization, not short-term cost control.
questions.explanationJa: 予算（消費）差異は、実際間接費と達成操業度に対する予算許容額を比べるため、いま対処すべき原価の超過を示す。操業度差異は、固定費率設定時の基準操業度と実際操業度がずれたことを表すにすぎず、示すのは設備の稼働度であって短期の原価統制ではない。

questions.stem:
The following were among Gage Co.'s April costs:
Normal spoilage | $ 5,000
Freight out | 10,000
Excess of actual manufacturing costs over standard costs | 20,000
Standard manufacturing costs | 100,000
Actual prime manufacturing costs | 80,000
Gage's April actual manufacturing overhead was
questions.explanation: Actual total manufacturing cost = standard $100,000 + excess of actual over standard $20,000 = $120,000. Prime cost (direct materials + direct labor) actually incurred was $80,000, so actual overhead = $120,000 - $80,000 = $40,000. Freight out is a selling expense and never enters manufacturing cost; normal spoilage is already inside the manufacturing total.
questions.explanationJa: 実際製造原価総額 = 標準 $100,000 + 標準超過額 $20,000 = $120,000。実際に発生した基本原価（直接材料＋直接労務）が $80,000 なので、実際製造間接費 = $120,000 − $80,000 = $40,000。発送費（freight out）は販売費であり製造原価に入らない。正常仕損は既に製造原価総額の中に含まれている。

questions.stem:
Tyro Co. uses a standard cost system. The following information pertains to direct labor for product B for the month of May:
Actual rate paid | $8.40 per hour
Standard rate | $8.00 per hour
Standard hours allowed for actual production | 2,000 hours
Labor efficiency variance | $800 unfavorable
What were the actual hours worked?
questions.explanation: The efficiency variance is measured at the standard rate: (actual hours - standard hours) x standard rate = $800 unfavorable. So (actual hours - 2,000) x $8.00 = $800, giving actual hours - 2,000 = 100 and actual hours = 2,100. The actual rate of $8.40 belongs to the rate variance and must not be used here.
questions.explanationJa: 能率差異は標準賃率で測る: (実際時間 − 標準時間) × 標準賃率 = $800 の不利差異。よって (実際時間 − 2,000) × $8.00 = $800 から 実際時間 − 2,000 = 100、実際時間 = 2,100時間。実際賃率 $8.40 は賃率差異で使う数値であり、ここで使ってはいけない。
questions.source: Proactive BAR CH53 Q.69 (code 1511) ※PDFの選択肢cは誤植(1,905)。Web版で2,095と確認し訂正

questions.stem: An increase in production levels within a relevant range most likely would result in

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increasing the variable cost per unit

choices.label: D
choices.text: Decreasing the variable cost per unit

questions.explanation: Within the relevant range, variable cost per unit and total fixed cost both stay constant by definition. Producing more units therefore adds variable cost and raises total cost. B, C and D each assert a change that the relevant-range assumption rules out.
questions.explanationJa: 関連範囲内では、単位あたり変動費と固定費総額はいずれも一定であるというのが前提。したがって生産量が増えれば変動費総額が増え、総原価が増加する。B・C・Dはいずれも、関連範囲の前提が否定している変化を述べている。

questions.stem: Kemper Company follows a practice of isolating variances at the earliest point in time. When is the appropriate time to isolate and recognize a direct material price variance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: When a purchase order is originated

choices.label: C
choices.text: When material is used in production

questions.explanation: Isolating variances as early as possible means recognizing the material price variance at purchase, when the price is determined and the purchasing decision can still be evaluated. Waiting until issue or use would delay the signal and mix the price effect with usage timing.
questions.explanationJa: 差異をできるだけ早い時点で把握するという方針では、材料価格差異は価格が確定する購入時点で認識する。この時点なら購買の意思決定を評価できる。払い出しや消費まで待つと、把握が遅れるうえ価格の影響と消費のタイミングが混ざる。

questions.stem: Virgil Corp. uses a standard cost system. In May, Virgil purchased and used 17,500 pounds of materials at a cost of $70,000. The materials usage variance was $2,500 unfavorable and the standard materials allowed for May production was 17,000 pounds. What was the materials price variance for May?
questions.explanation: First back out the standard price from the usage variance: (17,500 - 17,000) x standard price = $2,500, so standard price = $5.00. Actual price = $70,000 / 17,500 = $4.00. Price variance = ($4.00 - $5.00) x 17,500 = $17,500 favorable.

questions.stem: A company produces widgets with budgeted standard direct materials of 2 pounds per widget at $5 per pound. Standard direct labor was budgeted at 0.5 hour per widget at $15 per hour. The actual usage in the current year was 25,000 pounds and 3,000 hours to produce 10,000 widgets. What was the direct labor usage variance?
questions.explanation: Standard hours allowed = 10,000 widgets x 0.5 hour = 5,000. Usage (efficiency) variance = (actual hours - standard hours) x standard rate = (3,000 - 5,000) x $15 = $30,000 favorable. Fewer hours than standard were needed, so the variance is favorable. The material figures are not used in this variance.
questions.explanationJa: 標準許容時間 = 10,000個 × 0.5時間 = 5,000時間。労働時間（能率）差異 = (実際時間 − 標準時間) × 標準賃率 = (3,000 − 5,000) × $15 = $30,000 の有利差異。標準より少ない時間で済んだので有利となる。材料に関する数値はこの差異では使わない。

questions.stem: Management has reviewed the standard cost variance analysis and is trying to explain an unfavorable labor efficiency variance of $8,000. Which of the following is the most likely cause of the variance?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new labor contact increased wages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The maintenance of machinery has been inadequate for the last few months.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The department manager has chosen to use highly skilled workers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The quality of materials has improved greatly.

questions.explanation: An unfavorable labor efficiency variance means more hours were needed than standard. Poorly maintained machinery causes breakdowns and slow running, which consumes extra hours. A higher wage rate (A) shows up in the rate variance, not efficiency. Highly skilled workers (C) and better materials (D) would both tend to reduce hours and produce a favorable variance.
questions.explanationJa: 不利な労働能率差異は、標準より多くの時間を要したことを意味する。機械の保守不足は故障や能力低下を招き、余分な時間を消費させる。賃上げ（A）は能率差異ではなく賃率差異に現れる。熟練工の投入（C）や材料品質の向上（D）は、いずれも所要時間を減らす方向に働き有利差異を生みやすい。

questions.stem:
Yola Co. manufactures one product with a standard direct labor cost of four hours at $12.00 per hour.
During June, 1,000 units were produced using 4,100 hours at $12.20 per hour. The unfavorable direct labor efficiency variance was
questions.explanation: Standard hours allowed = 1,000 units x 4 hours = 4,000. Efficiency variance = (4,100 - 4,000) x standard rate $12.00 = $1,200 unfavorable. The actual rate of $12.20 belongs to the rate variance; using it here would give $1,220 (choice A).
questions.explanationJa: 標準許容時間 = 1,000個 × 4時間 = 4,000時間。能率差異 = (4,100 − 4,000) × 標準賃率 $12.00 = $1,200 の不利差異。実際賃率 $12.20 は賃率差異で使う数値で、ここで使うと $1,220（選択肢A）となり誤る。

questions.stem: The standard direct material cost to produce a unit of Lem is 4 meters at $2.50 per meter. During May, 4,200 meters of material costing $10,080 were purchased and used to produce 1,000 units of Lem. What was the material price variance for May?
questions.explanation: Price variance = actual cost - (actual quantity x standard price) = $10,080 - (4,200 x $2.50) = $10,080 - $10,500 = $420 favorable. The actual price works out to $10,080 / 4,200 = $2.40, below the $2.50 standard, confirming the favorable direction.
questions.explanationJa: 価格差異 = 実際購入額 − (実際数量 × 標準価格) = $10,080 − (4,200 × $2.50) = $10,080 − $10,500 = $420 の有利差異。実際価格は $10,080 ÷ 4,200 = $2.40 で標準 $2.50 を下回っており、有利であることが確かめられる。

questions.stem:
Under the two-variance method for analyzing overhead, which of the following variances consists of both variable and fixed overhead elements?
Controllable Volume variance (budget) variance
questions.explanation: Under two-variance analysis the controllable (budget) variance compares actual total overhead with the flexible budget allowance at standard hours, and that allowance contains both variable and fixed overhead. The volume variance measures only the under- or over-absorption of FIXED overhead caused by operating away from the denominator level.
questions.explanationJa: 2分法では、管理可能差異（予算差異）は実際間接費総額と標準許容時間における変動予算許容額を比べ、その許容額には変動費と固定費の両方が含まれる。一方の操業度差異は、基準操業度から離れた操業によって生じる「固定費」の配賦過不足だけを測る。

questions.stem:
Information on Wright Company's overhead costs for the June production activity is as follows:
Budgeted fixed overhead | $ 37,500
Standard fixed overhead rate per direct-labor hour | $ 3
Standard variable overhead rate per direct-labor hour | $ 6
Standard direct-labor hours allowed for actual production | 12,000
Actual total overhead incurred | $110,000
Wright has a standard absorption and flexible budgeting system, and uses the two-variance method (two- way analysis) for overhead variances. The volume (denominator) variance for June is
questions.explanation: The denominator (normal) hours implied by the fixed rate = $37,500 / $3 = 12,500 hours. Fixed overhead applied = 12,000 standard hours x $3 = $36,000. Volume variance = budgeted fixed $37,500 - applied $36,000 = $1,500 unfavorable, because actual production absorbed less fixed cost than budgeted. The variable rate and actual total overhead do not enter this variance.
questions.explanationJa: 固定費率から逆算した基準操業度 = $37,500 ÷ $3 = 12,500時間。固定費配賦額 = 標準許容時間 12,000時間 × $3 = $36,000。操業度差異 = 予算固定費 $37,500 − 配賦額 $36,000 = $1,500 の不利差異。実際生産が予算より少ない固定費しか吸収しなかったためである。変動費率と実際間接費総額はこの差異に関係しない。

questions.stem:
Under the two-variance method for analyzing factory overhead, which of the following is used in the computation of the controllable (budget) variance?
Budget allowance | Budget allowance
based on actual | based on standard
hours | hours
questions.explanation: The controllable (budget) variance is actual overhead less the budget allowance based on STANDARD hours allowed for the output achieved. The allowance based on actual hours appears in three-variance analysis, where it separates the spending and efficiency effects, but not in the two-variance method.
questions.explanationJa: 管理可能差異（予算差異）は、実際間接費から「達成した生産量に対する標準許容時間」に基づく予算許容額を差し引いて求める。実際時間に基づく予算許容額は3分法で消費差異と能率差異を分離するために使うもので、2分法では登場しない。

questions.stem: When using the two-variance method for analyzing factory overhead, the difference between the budget allowance based on standard hours allowed and the factory overhead applied to production is the
questions.explanation: The budget allowance at standard hours contains budgeted fixed overhead in full, while applied overhead charges fixed cost at the standard rate times standard hours. The gap between them is exactly the fixed overhead under- or over-absorbed, which is the volume variance.
questions.explanationJa: 標準許容時間における予算許容額には予算固定費が全額含まれるのに対し、配賦額は標準配賦率×標準許容時間で固定費を負担させる。この差はまさに固定費の配賦過不足であり、操業度差異にあたる。

questions.stem:
Columbia Company uses a standard cost system and prepared the following budget at normal capacity for the month of June:
Direct-labor hours | 12,000
Variable factory overhead | $24,000
Fixed factory overhead | $54,000
Total factory overhead per direct-labor hour | $6.50
Actual June direct labor hours worked | 11,000
Actual June total factory overhead | $73,500
Standard direct labor hours allowed for capacity attained in June | 10,500
Using the two-way analysis of overhead variances, what is the budget (controllable) variance for June?
questions.explanation: Variable rate = $24,000 / 12,000 hours = $2.00. Budget allowance at standard hours allowed = fixed $54,000 + (10,500 x $2.00) = $75,000. Controllable (budget) variance = actual $73,500 - $75,000 = $1,500 favorable. The 11,000 actual hours are not used in the two-variance method; the allowance is built on the 10,500 standard hours.
questions.explanationJa: 変動費率 = $24,000 ÷ 12,000時間 = $2.00。標準許容時間における予算許容額 = 固定費 $54,000 + (10,500時間 × $2.00) = $75,000。管理可能差異（予算差異）= 実際 $73,500 − $75,000 = $1,500 の有利差異。2分法では実際時間 11,000 は使わず、許容額は標準許容時間 10,500 で組む。

questions.stem:
Based on the following pertaining to Baby Frames, Inc., applicable to the month of May. Baby Frames evaluates manufacturing overhead by using variance analysis.
Actual | Budgeted
Number of frames manufactured | 19,000 | 20,000
Variable overhead costs | $ 4,100 | $2 per DL hour
Fixed overhead costs | $22,000 | $20,000; $1 per unit
Direct labor hours | 2,100 hours | 0.1 hour per frame
What is the variable overhead efficiency variance?
questions.explanation: Standard hours allowed = 19,000 frames x 0.1 hour = 1,900. The efficiency variance values the hours difference at the standard variable rate: (2,100 - 1,900) x $2 = $400 unfavorable. Actual variable overhead of $4,100 belongs to the spending variance.
questions.explanationJa: 標準許容時間 = 19,000個 × 0.1時間 = 1,900時間。能率差異は時間差を標準変動費率で評価する: (2,100 − 1,900) × $2 = $400 の不利差異。実際変動間接費 $4,100 は消費（予算）差異で使う数値。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information pertaining to Rand Company:
Units actually produced | 76,000
Actual direct labor hours worked | 160,000
Actual variable overhead incurred | $500,000
Actual fixed overhead incurred | 384,000
Based on monthly normal volume of 100,000 units (200,000 direct labor hours), Rand's standard cost system contains the following overhead costs:
Variable | $6 per unit
Fixed | $4 per unit
The fixed overhead budget variance was
questions.explanation: The fixed overhead budget (spending) variance compares actual fixed cost with BUDGETED fixed cost, ignoring volume. Budgeted fixed = 100,000 units x $4 = $400,000, actual = $384,000, so the variance is $16,000 favorable. The 76,000 units actually produced affect the volume variance, not this one.
questions.explanationJa: 固定費の予算（消費）差異は、実際固定費と「予算」固定費を比べ、生産量は考慮しない。予算固定費 = 100,000個 × $4 = $400,000、実際 $384,000 なので $16,000 の有利差異。実際生産量 76,000個 が影響するのは操業度差異であって、この差異ではない。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information pertaining to Rand Company:
Units actually produced | 76,000
Actual direct labor hours worked | 160,000
Actual variable overhead incurred | $500,000
Actual fixed overhead incurred | 384,000
Based on monthly normal volume of 100,000 units (200,000 direct labor hours), Rand's standard cost system contains the following overhead costs:
Variable | $6 per unit
Fixed | $4 per unit
The unfavorable variable overhead spending variance was
questions.explanation: Convert the per-unit rate to a per-hour rate: normal volume is 100,000 units for 200,000 hours, so 2 hours per unit and the variable rate is $6 / 2 = $3 per hour. Budget allowance at ACTUAL hours = 160,000 x $3 = $480,000. Spending variance = actual $500,000 - $480,000 = $20,000 unfavorable.
questions.explanationJa: 単位あたりの率を時間あたりに直す。基準操業度は 100,000個 で 200,000時間なので 1個あたり2時間、変動費率は $6 ÷ 2 = $3/時間。「実際時間」に基づく予算許容額 = 160,000時間 × $3 = $480,000。消費差異 = 実際 $500,000 − $480,000 = $20,000 の不利差異。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information pertaining to Rand Company:
Units actually produced | 76,000
Actual direct labor hours worked | 160,000
Actual variable overhead incurred | $500,000
Actual fixed overhead incurred | 384,000
Based on monthly normal volume of 100,000 units (200,000 direct labor hours), Rand's standard cost system contains the following overhead costs:
Variable | $6 per unit
Fixed | $4 per unit
The fixed overhead volume variance was
questions.explanation: Fixed overhead applied = 76,000 units actually produced x $4 = $304,000, while budgeted fixed overhead is 100,000 x $4 = $400,000. Volume variance = $400,000 - $304,000 = $96,000 unfavorable, reflecting that output fell well short of the normal volume used to set the rate.
questions.explanationJa: 固定費配賦額 = 実際生産量 76,000個 × $4 = $304,000。予算固定費は 100,000個 × $4 = $400,000。操業度差異 = $400,000 − $304,000 = $96,000 の不利差異。配賦率を決めた基準操業度に対し実際生産が大きく届かなかったことを示す。

questions.stem:
Under the three-variance method for analyzing factory overhead, which of the following is used in the computation of the spending variance?
Actual factory | Budget allowance
overhead | based on actual
hours
questions.explanation: Under three-variance analysis the spending variance is actual factory overhead less the budget allowance based on ACTUAL hours, so both figures are used. Splitting out the allowance at actual hours is precisely what separates spending from efficiency, which the two-variance method does not do.
questions.explanationJa: 3分法における消費差異は、実際製造間接費から「実際時間」に基づく予算許容額を差し引いて求めるため、両方の数値を使う。実際時間の予算許容額を切り出すことこそが、消費差異と能率差異を分離する仕組みであり、2分法にはこの区分がない。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information available from Rust company:
Actual factory overhead | $30,000
Fixed overhead, actual | $14,400
Fixed overhead, budgeted | $14,000
Actual hours | 7,000
Standard hours | 7,600
Variable overhead rate per direct-labor hour | $ 2.50
Rust uses a three-way analysis of overhead variances.
What is the spending variance?
questions.explanation: Budget allowance at actual hours = budgeted fixed $14,000 + (7,000 actual hours x $2.50) = $31,500. Spending variance = actual overhead $30,000 - $31,500 = $1,500 favorable. Note the allowance uses budgeted fixed cost ($14,000), not the actual fixed cost of $14,400.
questions.explanationJa: 実際時間に基づく予算許容額 = 予算固定費 $14,000 + (実際時間 7,000 × $2.50) = $31,500。消費差異 = 実際間接費 $30,000 − $31,500 = $1,500 の有利差異。許容額に使うのは「予算」固定費 $14,000 であり、実際固定費 $14,400 ではない点に注意。

questions.stem:
Based on the following information available from Rust company:
Actual factory overhead | $30,000
Fixed overhead, actual | $14,400
Fixed overhead, budgeted | $14,000
Actual hours | 7,000
Standard hours | 7,600
Variable overhead rate per direct-labor hour | $ 2.50
Rust uses a three-way analysis of overhead variances.
What is the efficiency variance?
questions.explanation: The efficiency variance isolates the hours difference at the variable rate only, since fixed cost does not change with hours: (7,000 actual - 7,600 standard) x $2.50 = $1,500 favorable. Fewer hours than standard were used, so the variance is favorable.
questions.explanationJa: 能率差異は変動費率だけで時間差を測る。固定費は時間に応じて変動しないためである: (実際 7,000 − 標準 7,600) × $2.50 = $1,500 の有利差異。標準より少ない時間で済んだので有利となる。

questions.stem:
A department's three-variance overhead standard costing system reported unfavorable spending and volume variances. The activity level selected for allocating overhead to the product was based on 80% of practical capacity. If 100% of practical capacity had been selected instead, how would the reported unfavorable spending and volume variances be affected?
Spending variance | Volume variance
questions.explanation: The spending variance compares actual overhead with the allowance at actual hours, and neither figure depends on the denominator level, so it is unchanged. Raising the denominator from 80% to 100% of practical capacity lowers the fixed rate and therefore the fixed overhead absorbed, widening the existing unfavorable volume variance.
questions.explanationJa: 消費差異は実際間接費と実際時間の予算許容額を比べるもので、どちらも基準操業度に依存しないため変化しない。基準操業度を実際的生産能力の80%から100%へ引き上げると固定費率が下がり、吸収される固定費が減るため、もともと不利であった操業度差異はさらに拡大する。

questions.stem:
Complex Company keeps inventory records using a FIFO cost flow assumption. Product enters Department B from Department A. Product conversion costs are incurred evenly in Department B, and material is added to the product at the end of the process. In May, there was no ending WIP inventory for Department B. In June, 3,000 units were transferred from Department A to Department B, at a total cost of $7,500. At the end of June, 1,000 units were finished and 2,000 units were 40% complete. During June, $9,000 was incurred for conversion costs and $500 for material costs in Department B. Department C is unrelated to Department A and B. in Department C, Complex produces two products, Y and Z, from the same raw material. Joint product costs are $900. The process yields 200 units of Y and 400 units of Z. Sales values at split-off are estimated to be $5 and $3.50 per unit, respectively.
What are the equivalent units of production for conversion and material costs for Department B for June?
Conversion | Material
questions.explanation: Conversion is incurred evenly, so ending WIP counts at its completion: 1,000 finished + 2,000 x 40% (800) = 1,800. Material is added at the END of the process, so units still in process have received none: only the 1,000 finished units count. Hence 1,800 and 1,000.
questions.explanationJa: 加工費は工程を通じて平均的に発生するため、期末仕掛品は完成度分だけ数える: 完成 1,000 + 2,000 × 40%（800）= 1,800。材料は工程の「終点」で投入されるので、仕掛中の単位にはまだ投入されていない。したがって材料の換算量は完成した 1,000単位のみ。よって 1,800 と 1,000。

questions.stem:
Complex Company keeps inventory records using a FIFO cost flow assumption. Product enters Department B from Department A. Product conversion costs are incurred evenly in Department B, and material is added to the product at the end of the process. In May, there was no ending WIP inventory for Department B. In June, 3,000 units were transferred from Department A to Department B, at a total cost of $7,500. At the end of June, 1,000 units were finished and 2,000 units were 40% complete. During June, $9,000 was incurred for conversion costs and $500 for material costs in Department B. Department C is unrelated to Department A and B. in Department C, Complex produces two products, Y and Z, from the same raw material. Joint product costs are $900. The process yields 200 units of Y and 400 units of Z. Sales values at split-off are estimated to be $5 and $3.50 per unit, respectively.
What is the unit cost of WIP inventory in Department B at the end of June?
questions.explanation: Transferred-in cost per unit = $7,500 / 3,000 = $2.50. Conversion cost per equivalent unit = $9,000 / 1,800 = $5.00. Ending WIP units carry full transferred-in cost but only 40% of conversion, and no material because material enters at the end: $2.50 + ($5.00 x 40%) = $4.50 per unit.
questions.explanationJa: 前工程費の単価 = $7,500 ÷ 3,000単位 = $2.50。加工費の換算単位あたり原価 = $9,000 ÷ 1,800 = $5.00。期末仕掛品は前工程費を全額負担するが、加工費は40%分のみ、材料は終点投入のため負担しない: $2.50 + ($5.00 × 40%) = 1単位あたり $4.50。

questions.stem:
Complex Company keeps inventory records using a FIFO cost flow assumption. Product enters Department B from Department A. Product conversion costs are incurred evenly in Department B, and material is added to the product at the end of the process. In May, there was no ending WIP inventory for Department B. In June, 3,000 units were transferred from Department A to Department B, at a total cost of $7,500. At the end of June, 1,000 units were finished and 2,000 units were 40% complete. During June, $9,000 was incurred for conversion costs and $500 for material costs in Department B. Department C is unrelated to Department A and B. in Department C, Complex produces two products, Y and Z, from the same raw material. Joint product costs are $900. The process yields 200 units of Y and 400 units of Z. Sales values at split-off are estimated to be $5 and $3.50 per unit, respectively.
What is the total cost of the finished goods from Department B in June?
questions.explanation: Finished units absorb all three cost elements in full. Material cost per unit = $500 / 1,000 = $0.50. Unit cost of finished goods = transferred-in $2.50 + conversion $5.00 + material $0.50 = $8.00, so 1,000 units x $8.00 = $8,000.
questions.explanationJa: 完成品は3つの原価要素をすべて全額負担する。材料費の単価 = $500 ÷ 1,000単位 = $0.50。完成品の単位原価 = 前工程費 $2.50 + 加工費 $5.00 + 材料費 $0.50 = $8.00。したがって 1,000単位 × $8.00 = $8,000。

questions.stem:
Complex Company keeps inventory records using a FIFO cost flow assumption. Product enters Department B from Department A. Product conversion costs are incurred evenly in Department B, and material is added to the product at the end of the process. In May, there was no ending WIP inventory for Department B. In June, 3,000 units were transferred from Department A to Department B, at a total cost of $7,500. At the end of June, 1,000 units were finished and 2,000 units were 40% complete. During June, $9,000 was incurred for conversion costs and $500 for material costs in Department B. Department C is unrelated to Department A and B. in Department C, Complex produces two products, Y and Z, from the same raw material. Joint product costs are $900. The process yields 200 units of Y and 400 units of Z. Sales values at split-off are estimated to be $5 and $3.50 per unit, respectively.
What is the amount of joint costs to allocate to each product in Department C on the basis of relative sales value at split-off?
Product Y | Product Z
questions.explanation: Relative sales value at split-off: Y = 200 x $5.00 = $1,000, Z = 400 x $3.50 = $1,400, total $2,400. Y takes $900 x ($1,000 / $2,400) = $375 and Z takes $900 x ($1,400 / $2,400) = $525. Allocating on units (200:400) would instead give $300 and $600, which is choice A.

questions.stem:
A processing department produces joint products Ajac and Bjac, each of which incurs separable production costs after split-off. Information concerning a batch produced at a $60,000 joint cost before split-off follows:
Product | Separable costs | Sales value
Ajac | $ 8,000 | $ 80,000
Bjac | 22,000 | 40,000
Total | $30,000 | $120,00
What is the joint cost assigned to Ajac if costs are assigned using the relative net realizable value?
questions.explanation: Net realizable value = sales value less separable costs. Ajac = $80,000 - $8,000 = $72,000, Bjac = $40,000 - $22,000 = $18,000, total $90,000. Ajac's share = $60,000 x ($72,000 / $90,000) = $48,000. Using sales value alone ($80,000 of $120,000) would give $40,000, which ignores that Bjac needs far more separable cost.

questions.stem:
Mason Company uses a job-order cost system and applies manufacturing overhead to jobs using a predetermined overhead rate based on direct-labor dollars. The rate for the current year is 200 percent of direct-labor dollars. This rate was calculated last December and will be used throughout the current year. Mason had one job, No. 150, in process on August 1 with raw materials costs of $2,000 and direct- labor costs of $3,000. During August, raw materials and direct labor added to jobs were as follows:
No.150 | No.151 | No.152
Raw materials | -- | $4,000 | $1,000
Direct labor | $1,500 | 5,000 | 2,500
Actual manufacturing overhead for the month of August was $20,000. During the month, Mason completed job Nos. 150 and 151. For August, manufacturing overhead was
questions.explanation: Overhead is applied at 200% of direct labor dollars incurred during August: ($1,500 + $5,000 + $2,500) x 200% = $9,000 x 2 = $18,000. Actual overhead was $20,000, so overhead is underapplied by $2,000. Whether jobs were completed does not affect the amount applied.
questions.explanationJa: 間接費は8月に発生した直接労務費の200%で配賦する: ($1,500 + $5,000 + $2,500) × 200% = $9,000 × 2 = $18,000。実際発生額は $20,000 なので、$2,000 の配賦不足となる。どのジョブが完成したかは配賦額に影響しない。
